<!-- name: Detection Intel -->
<!-- board: See why each detection matched | Tune alerts by type/device | Smarter Remote ID + Flock | RSSI trend + tracker spam guard -->

**Detection Intelligence.** v1.21.0 makes SquachWatch much more explicit about
*why* something was detected, *how often* it has been seen, *whether it is
moving closer or farther away*, and *what the device should do about that
specific target*. It also adds stronger drone / Remote ID and Flock recognition,
tracker-spam suppression, clearer ignored-device state, richer T-Watch haptic
controls, and more complete BlackBox console forensics.

This file is a **release-notes draft**. The repository VERSION remains 1.20.1
until the remaining v1.21 hardware regression gates are completed and an
explicit release is approved.

**Added**
- **Concrete detection evidence.** Live detections now record the actual match
  source: BLE manufacturer ID, service UUID, advertised name, Find My payload,
  iBeacon payload, Wi-Fi OUI, SSID, Pwnagotchi, evil-twin, deauthentication,
  or Remote ID evidence. ALERT, LOG and MORE INFO expose that source instead
  of forcing the user to infer why a classification happened.
- **~15-second RSSI history and trend.** Each live detection keeps eight
  allocation-free RSSI samples. LOG shows compact live direction plus a mini
  sparkline where the layout has room. HUNT uses the same shared movement
  classifier with GETTING WARMER / HOLDING STEADY / GETTING COLDER guidance,
  while ALERT stays focused on immediate detection facts.
- **Uniform sighting counts.** A dedicated saturating repeat counter gives alert
  rules a consistent meaning across BLE, Wi-Fi and deauth. Deauth keeps raw
  frame count in `hits` while `repeats` counts qualifying bursts, so one noisy
  burst cannot masquerade as multiple independent sightings.
- **Per-type Alert Rules.** Every detection type can independently choose full
  alert or LOG ONLY, inherit or override the global confidence threshold,
  require 1/2/3/5 sightings, use OFF/30s/1m/5m/15m cooldown, and decide whether
  a normal signature alert may wake a sleeping display. Defaults preserve the
  previous v1.20.1 behavior.
- **Device Policies.** Persistent NORMAL / IGNORE / TRUSTED / ALWAYS ALERT
  behavior replaces the old IGNORE-only model. IGNORE and TRUSTED continue to
  count and log detections while suppressing interruption. ALWAYS ALERT can
  bypass per-type log-only/confidence/repeat/cooldown rules plus device snooze
  and AUTO SNOOZE, but it does not override DETECTION FILTER or lock-screen
  alert security.
- **Chronological EVENTS history.** LOG now switches between the existing
  one-row-per-device DEVICES view and an EVENTS view showing every persisted
  FIRST/BACK sighting newest-first. Event rows include time, type, MAC, RSSI,
  confidence, hit count, identity, current HERE/GONE state, and current
  non-normal policy when applicable.
- **Read-only historical EVENTS.** WATCH/HUNT/policy long-press actions remain
  DEVICES-only, preventing an old historical row from being mistaken for a
  currently actionable live device.
- **Remote ID detection.** BLE OpenDroneID Service Data and Wi-Fi Remote ID
  beacon/NAN paths are recognized structurally instead of relying only on
  generic vendor identity. The manufacturer table also adds verified drone
  makers including DJI, Parrot, Skydio, Teal, Freefly, AeroVironment,
  PowerVision, Zipline, Autel, Hubsan, Yuneec, Quantum Systems,
  Inspired Flight, FIMI and HOVERAir / Zero Zero.
- **Refreshed Flock recognition.** The stale generic Flock guesses were
  replaced with the current 32 field-observed prefixes plus the Flock-owned
  `B4:1E:52` block. Empty-SSID wildcard probes strengthen field-prefix evidence,
  and the generic Qualcomm `00:03:7F` prefix is accepted only when paired with
  Flock-like wildcard-probe behavior. Penguin battery names and the existing
  external-battery identifier are recognized without blanket-classifying
  generic Qualcomm or Bluetooth names.
- **Tracker spam-flood suppression.** AirTag, Samsung SmartTag, Google Find My
  Device tracker and Tile detections now feed a tracker-only flood guard for
  BLE spam tools that rotate through fresh identities. Roughly eight quick,
  short-lived one-visit identities, or 40 genuinely new tracker identities in
  one minute, can mark a flood. One explanatory alert is allowed; later
  matching identities continue to LOG without repeated screen takeover. WATCH
  and ALWAYS ALERT remain explicit per-device exceptions.
- **BLACKBOX full forensic dump.** The serial BLACKBOX command now walks through
  CLR markers and can show records that the normal on-device LOG correctly
  hides after a clear. The LOG iterator and its clear-history behavior are
  unchanged.

**Changed**
- **Ignored state is visible.** LOG > DEVICES now shows an IGNORED/IGN marker,
  and the device action changes from IGNORE to UNIGNORE when appropriate.
- **T-Watch settings cleanup.** Watch-only controls now live on a dedicated
  WATCH SETTINGS page. BUZZ is OFF / HIGH / MED / LOW instead of a single
  ON/OFF toggle; an existing OFF stays OFF and an existing ON migrates to MED.
  Enabled levels play a sample and use the DRV2605 effect/drive settings
  appropriate to the selected strength.
- WATCH keeps its existing special behavior and remains separate from ALWAYS
  ALERT. It still bypasses AUTO SNOOZE through the dedicated WATCH alert path,
  but does not become a blanket bypass for confidence, repeat, cooldown, or
  LOG ONLY rules.
- SpamWatch is suppression only: it cannot create an alert that DETECTION
  FILTER, per-type rules, confidence/repeat thresholds, cooldown, Device
  Policies, AUTO SNOOZE or lock-screen rules would have blocked. Suppressed
  flood identities also do not consume AUTO SNOOZE allowance.
- DESK mode keeps its compact detection card. The first tracker-flood
  announcement adds a TRACKER SPAM toast there instead of forcing the full
  ALERT layout.
- Cooldown and fresh-event handling reuse the existing alert bookkeeping rather
  than adding another timestamp to every live `Detection`.
- LOG's DEVICES and EVENTS views share the existing BlackBox page buffer. There
  is no second timeline database or duplicate resident history cache.
- Device policy records are compact fixed 8-byte entries (MAC + type + policy)
  instead of reserving alias storage for every row.
- The LOG sparkline remains opportunistic: names and timestamps win on narrow
  240-pixel layouts, so the chart disappears rather than overlapping identity
  text.
- Historical BlackBox records remain honest about their limits: evidence and
  RSSI history were not stored by older rows and are not reconstructed or
  invented after reboot.

**Migration and compatibility**
- Existing v1.20.1 per-device IGNORE records migrate into the new policy format.
  Both the typed `dev` format and older MAC-only `macs` format are supported.
- Migration is transactional: legacy keys are removed only after the complete
  new-format write succeeds, and failed writes leave the source data intact.
- Existing T-Watch BUZZ OFF migrates to OFF; existing BUZZ ON migrates to MED.
  The new four-state selection is stored separately.
- BlackBox record format, SD CSV format, and the existing detection-history
  storage remain unchanged.
- The normal 3.2-inch CYD/ST7798 profile, its optional 80 MHz display variant,
  Freenove 3.2-inch, AWOK 2.4-inch, RL Phantom 2.4-inch, 2.8-inch CYD variants,
  and LilyGo T-Watch S3 beta remain in the release matrix.
- **BLE OTA remains available in this fork.** The later upstream optimization
  that removes the BLE OTA GATT peripheral from most non-watch boards was
  intentionally not ported. USB/browser flash and Wi-Fi OTA remain available
  as before as well.
- No new production tag is created by these changes, and the existing
  v1.20.1 tag/release remains untouched.

**Validation**
- Detection-intelligence Stages A-E were developed as separate reviewed changes
  with full firmware, host-test and native/WASM emulator regression gates.
- The later Remote ID, ignore-state, Flock, T-Watch settings, BlackBox and
  SpamWatch changes were also merged independently after full host/emulator/UI
  and firmware-board-matrix validation.
- Current master `9ad7e0c24d63f4fd94bd8fcf72a41ad2fe298c7a` passed post-merge
  Build #156: host tests, native emulator, UI screenshot regression, and the
  complete firmware board matrix all passed.
- The earlier 3.2-inch CYD/ST7798 lab migration/basic validation and Stage B/C
  alert-policy validation passed. Those already-completed checks should not be
  repeated solely because of later narrow changes.
- The remaining release gate is the manual v1.21 hardware regression checklist,
  including the outstanding T-Watch hardware pass, persistence / BlackBox / SD
  regression checks, and final soak validation.
- OTA firmware continues to use the fork's signing pipeline; the production
  v1.20.1 release/tag is not modified by this draft.

**Release status**
- Public production release: **v1.20.1**
- v1.21 feature set: **merged on master, unreleased**
- Repository VERSION: **1.20.1**
- No v1.21.0 tag or GitHub release should be created until the remaining
  hardware regression checklist is complete and release approval is explicit.
